questions.question: Which DSE IV events are genuinely single entry (freezeout) - one buy-in, no re-entry, no add-on?
questions.known: All 37 official structure sheets print the buy-in, house fee, prize-pool share, guarantee, chips, level duration and late-registration window. None of them prints an entry-count rule. The multi-flight sheets do contain 'Any player who bags chips for Day 2 may not play a subsequent flight', which implies more than one entry is possible for those events.
questions.unknown: The maximum number of entries per player for every single event number.
questions.blocks: Everything. The single-entry filter, the ranking, and the trip budget all depend on it.
questions.howToResolve: Email lv_cas_poker@venetianlasvegas.com or call 702.414.7657 and ask for the written maximum-entry policy per event number. Ask specifically: 'Is event #N a single-entry freezeout, or may a player who busts buy in again?' Get it in writing (email) before booking.

questions.question: What are your exact travel dates and how many nights?
questions.known: DSE IV runs November 16 - December 23, 2026. The two densest stretches are Dec 3-6 ($800, $500K GTD, six flights) and Dec 17-20 ($1,100, $500K GTD, five flights plus the final).
questions.unknown: Your arrival date, departure date and therefore the number of nights and the set of events you can reach.
questions.blocks: Hotel quotes, the total trip cost, and which events are even candidates.
questions.howToResolve: Pick dates. Every hotel row links an official booking page; open it with your dates to get an itemised total.

questions.question: What is the true cost per night for each candidate hotel for those dates?
questions.known: Venetian resort fee is $55 plus tax per night (S06). Clark County Room Tax is 13.38% and is excluded from quoted daily rates (S08). Venetian self-parking is $20/day for registered guests, $40/day valet, and free for poker players who play 3+ hours (S09). The Venetian poker rate starts at $119 or $209 and requires 6 hours live cash or a $300+ tournament buy-in per night (S07).
questions.unknown: The date-specific nightly base rate for every hotel, and the resort fee for all hotels except the Venetian.
questions.blocks: Any true like-for-like hotel comparison and the total trip cost.
questions.howToResolve: Open each official booking link on the Hotels page for your dates, capture the itemised total (base + resort fee + tax), and log it in the rate log on this site. Use the same dates, occupancy and room category for every hotel.

questions.question: What is your total budget, and how do you want it split between buy-ins and the room?
questions.known: Entry costs range from $100 (satellites, excluded) to $2,200. Among single-day events the range is $200 to $1,100. The Venetian poker rate can be as low as $119/night but only with qualifying play.
questions.blocks: Whether to optimise for one big event or many small ones.
questions.howToResolve: Use the Trip Cost calculator on this site: entries x buy-in + nights x true nightly cost. Set a number and the Events page can be sorted within it.

questions.question: Do bounty events count as 'single entry' for you?
questions.known: Bounty, PKO and Kings-and-Queens events pay a cash bounty per elimination. The buy-in is a single price; no sheet offers a paid chip add-on. Their guarantee is printed as 'prize pool + total bounties' so the two are mixed in one number.
questions.unknown: Whether you consider a bounty a form of paying for advantage. It is not - it is a payout format - but the guarantee figure is not comparable with a freezeout guarantee.
questions.howToResolve: Decide yes or no. This site labels every bounty row and keeps the ratio column separate so you can switch the filter on the Events page.

questions.question: Do you want to start at 8:00 AM?
questions.known: No DSE IV event starts before 9:10 AM, and 9:10 AM is a satellite. The earliest non-satellite start is 10:10 AM. The Venetian poker room is open 24 hours daily (S05).
questions.unknown: Whether an 8 AM start matters to you.
questions.howToResolve: Either accept a 10:10 AM first event, or plan 8:00-10:00 AM as cash game time. Do not plan around an 8 AM tournament - none exists in the official schedule.

questions.question: How many events per day do you want, and are you willing to play two?
questions.known: Most days have a morning/afternoon event and an evening event. Registration windows usually do not overlap: morning events close registration around 3:40-4:55 PM and evening events start at 5:10 PM.
questions.unknown: Whether you will actually be finished with the first event in time. No official source publishes a finish time or a field size, so this cannot be computed.
questions.howToResolve: Treat the evening event as a conditional fallback, not a plan. Register for it only after you are out of the first event. Ask the poker room for typical finish times.

questions.question: Are you 50 or over? Are you female?
questions.known: Events 24 and 32 ($600 Seniors) require players to be 50+; the sheet says anyone under 50 forfeits both prize money and the buy-in. Event 39 ($800 LIPS Ladies, 2Day) requires players to be female and 21+. Events 33 and 37 ($100 LIPS satellites) are open to female players only. Events 35, 43 and the LIPS events withhold an extra $10 or $20 flat fee for Ladies International Poker Series.
questions.howToResolve: Tick the eligibility boxes on the Events page; ineligible rows are greyed out.

questions.question: Will you have a car?
questions.known: Venetian self-parking is $20/day for registered hotel guests and complimentary for poker players who play 3+ hours per day (supervisor must confirm). Valet is $40/day. Complimentary self-parking is also free while playing.
questions.unknown: Whether parking is a line item for you.
questions.blocks: A small but real part of the daily cost, and whether hotels beyond comfortable walking range become viable.
questions.howToResolve: If you are playing 3+ hours a day, budget $0 for parking at the Venetian. Otherwise budget $20/day.

questions.question: Should the plan extend past December 23 into the NYE series or the January Showdown?
questions.known: DeepStack Extravaganza NYE runs December 24, 2026 - January 10, 2027 (more than $1.1M guaranteed; $2,200 $300K GTD Dec 27-31; $1,600 MSPT $400K GTD Jan 1-4). DeepStack Showdown (January) runs January 11 - February 14, 2027 (more than $2.2M guaranteed). Neither series had a structure sheet read this session.
questions.unknown: Whether your trip extends into either series.
questions.blocks: Whether those events need to be researched.
questions.howToResolve: Say yes or no. If yes, each series' schedule and structure sheets need the same full read that DSE IV got.

questions.question: Do you want any non-Venetian Strip poker rooms included?
questions.known: This session verified the Venetian in full. Prior sessions recorded that Wynn WPT events and Bellagio weekly events carry re-entry or rebuy wording, and that ARIA's poker guide is undated; those were not re-verified here. Wynn's official fee pages are currently unreachable.
questions.unknown: Whether a wider scan is wanted, and whether those rooms' events would survive a single-entry filter.
questions.howToResolve: Say yes or no. A wider scan means fetching each room's official schedule and reading each event's structure sheet.

questions.question: Do you have a Venetian Rewards card?
questions.known: Every structure sheet requires players to be 21+ and to hold a Venetian Rewards card to participate. The poker rate is tracked through that card, and it earns $2/hour in rewards redeemable at resort outlets and toward tournament buy-ins.
questions.blocks: Registration itself, and access to the poker room rate.
questions.howToResolve: Sign up at venetianlasvegas.com/venetianrewards. Bring the number when you book the poker rate (code EPOKR25, 866.255.8936).
